</td><td>

A formatter for numeric values with comma-separated formatting.

The `CommasFormatter` class formats numbers with commas as thousands separators, providing better readability for large numbers. It supports various customization options such as decimal precision, units, and locale.

</td><td>

A formatter for numeric values.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

</td><td>

A formatter for percentage values.

The `PercentFormatter` class formats numeric values as percentages by multiplying the input value by 100. It supports customization options like decimal precision, locale, and more for tailored output.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

</td><td>

Thrown when registry registration attempts to replace an existing primitive value.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[ShortFormatter](#morpho-ts.shortformatter)


</td><td>

A formatter for compact numeric values.

The `ShortFormatter` class formats numbers in a short or compact notation, such as `1.2k` for thousands or `3.4M` for millions. It is useful for presenting large numbers in a concise and readable manner. This formatter supports customization options like decimal precision, units, and readability for small values.


</td></tr>

<a name="morpho-ts._try"></a>

## \_try() function

Runs an async accessor and returns `undefined` for expected lookup errors.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare function _try<T, ErrorClasses extends readonly ErrorClass[] = []>(accessor: () => Promise<T>, ...errorClasses: ErrorClasses): Promise<T | undefined>;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

accessor


</td><td>

() =&gt; Promise&lt;T&gt;


</td><td>

Async accessor to run.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

errorClasses


</td><td>

ErrorClasses


</td><td>

Optional error classes to catch. When omitted, all errors are caught.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

Promise&lt;T \| undefined&gt;

The accessor result, or `undefined` when the accessor throws a matching error.

## Example


```ts
import { _try, UnknownAddressError } from "@morpho-org/morpho-ts";

const address = await _try(async () => {
  throw new UnknownAddressError({ chainId: 1, label: "midnight" });
}, UnknownAddressError);
console.log(address);
```

<a name="morpho-ts._try_1"></a>

## \_try() function

Runs a sync accessor and returns `undefined` for expected lookup errors.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare function _try<T, ErrorClasses extends readonly ErrorClass[] = []>(accessor: () => T, ...errorClasses: ErrorClasses): T | undefined;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

accessor


</td><td>

() =&gt; T


</td><td>

Sync accessor to run.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

errorClasses


</td><td>

ErrorClasses


</td><td>

Optional error classes to catch. When omitted, all errors are caught.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

T \| undefined

The accessor result, or `undefined` when the accessor throws a matching error.

## Example


```ts
import { _try, UnknownAddressError } from "@morpho-org/morpho-ts";

const address = _try(() => {
  throw new UnknownAddressError({ chainId: 1, label: "midnight" });
}, UnknownAddressError);
console.log(address);
```


<a name="morpho-ts.baseformatter.createof"></a>

## BaseFormatter.createOf() method

Creates a bound version of the `of` method, retaining the current formatter options.

**Signature:**

```typescript
createOf(): {
        <T extends bigint | null | undefined, D extends number | null | undefined>(value: T, decimals: D): Exclude<T, bigint> | Exclude<D, number> | string;
        <T extends number | null | undefined>(value: T): Exclude<T, number> | string;
    };
```
**Returns:**

{ &lt;T extends bigint \| null \| undefined, D extends number \| null \| undefined&gt;(value: T, decimals: D): Exclude&lt;T, bigint&gt; \| Exclude&lt;D, number&gt; \| string; &lt;T extends number \| null \| undefined&gt;(value: T): Exclude&lt;T, number&gt; \| string; }

A bound `of` function.

<a name="morpho-ts.baseformatter.default"></a>

## BaseFormatter.default() method

Sets a default value for the formatter. If the provided value is `undefined` or `null`<!-- -->, the method returns the current instance without modifying it. Otherwise, it creates a new formatter instance with the specified default value.

**Signature:**

```typescript
default(_d: string): FormatterWithDefault<this>;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

\_d


</td><td>

string


</td><td>

The default value to set. Accepts a string or `undefined`<!-- -->/`null`<!-- -->.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

FormatterWithDefault&lt;this&gt;

A new formatter instance with the updated default value, or the current instance if `_d` is `undefined` or `null`<!-- -->.

## Remarks

Overloads:

- `default(_d: string): FormatterWithDefault<this>;` - `default(_d: string | undefined | null): this;`

## Example

const formatter = new Formatter(); const updatedFormatter = formatter.default("N/A");

console.log(updatedFormatter.of(null)); // Outputs: "N/A"

<a name="morpho-ts.baseformatter.of"></a>

## BaseFormatter.of() method

Formats a given value according to the formatter's configuration.

**Signature:**

```typescript
of<T extends bigint | null | undefined, D extends number | null | undefined>(value: T, decimals: D): Exclude<T, bigint> | Exclude<D, number> | string;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

value


</td><td>

T


</td><td>

The value to format. It can be: - A `bigint` for precise numeric representation. - A `number` for floating-point or scientific notation input. - `null` or `undefined`<!-- -->, in which case the method will retain the nullability of the input unless a default value is set.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

decimals


</td><td>

D


</td><td>

If input value is a bigint. It can be `null` or `undefined`<!-- -->, in which case the method will retain the nullability of the input unless a default value is set.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

Exclude&lt;T, bigint&gt; \| Exclude&lt;D, number&gt; \| string

The formatted value as a string, or: - The default value `value` or `decimals` is `null` or `undefined`<!-- -->. - `null`<!-- -->or `undefined` in case `value` or `decimals` is `null` or `undefined` and no default value is set

## Example 1

// Example with bigint input console.log(formatter.of(123456789n, 2)); // Output: "1234567.89"

## Example 2

// Example with number input console.log(formatter.of(123.45)); // Output: "123.45"

## Example 3

// Handling null or undefined console.log(formatter.of(null, 2)); // Output: null

<a name="morpho-ts.bigintcomparator"></a>

## bigIntComparator() function

Creates a comparator for sorting by nullable bigint keys.

**Signature:**

```typescript
bigIntComparator: <T>(getter: (x: T) => bigint | undefined | null, order?: "asc" | "desc") => (a: T, b: T) => -1 | 0 | 1
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

getter


</td><td>

(x: T) =&gt; bigint \| undefined \| null


</td><td>

Reads the bigint sort key from an item.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

order


</td><td>

"asc" \| "desc"


</td><td>

_(Optional)_ Optional sort order. Defaults to ascending.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

(a: T, b: T) =&gt; -1 \| 0 \| 1

A comparator compatible with `Array.prototype.sort`<!-- -->.

## Example


```ts
import { bigIntComparator } from "@morpho-org/morpho-ts";

const sorted = [{ value: 2n }, { value: 1n }].sort(
  bigIntComparator((item) => item.value),
);
// [{ value: 1n }, { value: 2n }]
```

<a name="morpho-ts.commasformatter"></a>

## CommasFormatter class

A formatter for numeric values with comma-separated formatting.

The `CommasFormatter` class formats numbers with commas as thousands separators, providing better readability for large numbers. It supports various customization options such as decimal precision, units, and locale.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare class CommasFormatter extends CommonFormatter
```
**Extends:** [CommonFormatter](#morpho-ts.commonformatter)

## Example 1

// Basic usage const formatter = formatter; console.log(formatter.of(1234567.89)); // Output: "1,234,567.89"

## Example 2

// Customizing decimal places const formatterWithDigits = formatter.digits(2); console.log(formatterWithDigits.of(1234567.89)); // Output: "1,234,567.89"

## Example 3

// Adding a unit const formatterWithUnit = formatter.unit("$"); console.log(formatterWithUnit.of(1234567.89)); // Output: "$1,234,567.89"

```typescript
digits(_d: number | undefined | null): this;
```

number \| undefined \| null

<a name="morpho-ts.commonformatter.locale"></a>

## CommonFormatter.locale() method

Sets the locale for the formatted output.

This method configures the formatter to format numbers according to the specified locale, which can affect decimal symbols, thousand separators, and other locale-specific formatting rules.

If `_l` is `null` or `undefined`<!-- -->, the current instance is returned without modification.

**Signature:**

```typescript
locale(_l: string | undefined | null): this;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

\_l


</td><td>

string \| undefined \| null


</td><td>

The locale identifier (e.g., `"en-US"`<!-- -->, `"fr-FR"`<!-- -->, `"de-DE"`<!-- -->) to use for formatting. Can be `null` or `undefined`<!-- -->.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

this

A new formatter instance with the `locale` option set to the specified locale, or the current instance if `_l` is `null` or `undefined`<!-- -->.

## Example

const updatedFormatter = formatter.locale("fr-FR"); console.log(updatedFormatter.of(1234.56)); // Output: "1 234,56" (French locale)

const usFormatter = formatter.locale("en-US"); console.log(usFormatter.of(1234.56)); // Output: "1,234.56" (US locale)

Enables the inclusion of a sign (+/-) in the formatted output.

This method configures the formatter to explicitly display a positive sign (`+`<!-- -->) for positive values, and a negative sign (`-`<!-- -->) for negative values. By default, positive values are displayed without a sign.

```typescript
sign(): this;
```
**Returns:**

this

A new formatter instance with the `sign` option set to `true`<!-- -->.

## Example

Enables or disables trailing zeros in the formatted output.

This method modifies the formatter's configuration to remove or keep unnecessary trailing zeros from decimal numbers based on the `enable` parameter. A new formatter instance is created with this option enabled or disabled.

This method configures the formatter to append or prepend a unit symbol to the formatted value. Common examples include currency symbols (`$`<!-- -->), percentage symbols (`%`<!-- -->), or custom units.

If `_u` is `null` or `undefined`<!-- -->, the current instance is returned without modification.

**Signature:**

```typescript
unit(_u: string | undefined | null): this;
```

<a name="morpho-ts.createformat"></a>

## createFormat() function

Creates a set of pre-configured formatters for various numeric formats.

The `createFormat` function generates formatters for hex, number, commas-separated, short, and percentage formats. It allows setting default options for all formatters and defining custom formatters for specific use cases.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare function createFormat<TCustom extends Record<string, FormatNumberOptions | FormatShortOptions | FormatPercentOptions | FormatCommasOptions | FormatHexOptions> & {
    [K in keyof TDefaultOptions]?: never;
} = {}>(defaultOptions?: Partial<TDefaultOptions>, customFormatters?: TCustom): {
    readonly hex: HexFormatter;
    readonly number: NumberFormatter;
    readonly commas: CommasFormatter;
    readonly short: ShortFormatter;
    readonly percent: PercentFormatter;
} & { readonly [K in keyof TCustom]: TFormatters[TCustom[K]["format"]]; };
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

defaultOptions


</td><td>

Partial&lt;TDefaultOptions&gt;


</td><td>

_(Optional)_ Default options to apply to all formatters or specific format types.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

customFormatters


</td><td>

TCustom


</td><td>

_(Optional)_ An object defining additional custom formatters with specific configurations.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

{ readonly hex: [HexFormatter](#morpho-ts.hexformatter)<!-- -->; readonly number: [NumberFormatter](#morpho-ts.numberformatter)<!-- -->; readonly commas: [CommasFormatter](#morpho-ts.commasformatter)<!-- -->; readonly short: [ShortFormatter](#morpho-ts.shortformatter)<!-- -->; readonly percent: [PercentFormatter](#morpho-ts.percentformatter)<!-- -->; } &amp; { readonly \[K in keyof TCustom\]: TFormatters\[TCustom\[K\]\["format"\]\]; }

An object containing pre-configured formatters and custom formatters if provided.

## Example 1

// Create default formatters const format = createFormat(); console.log(format.number.of(1234.56)); // Output: "1234.56" console.log(format.commas.of(1234.56)); // Output: "1,234.56"

## Example 2

// Create formatters with default options const format = createFormat(<!-- -->{ all: { digits: 2 }<!-- -->, number: { unit: "$" }<!-- -->, }<!-- -->); console.log(format.number.of(1234.56)); // Output: "$1234.56" console.log(format.short.of(1234567.89)); // Output: "1.23M"

## Example 3

// Adding custom formatters const format = createFormat(<!-- -->{<!-- -->}<!-- -->, { customHex: { format: Format.hex, prefix: true } }<!-- -->); console.log(format.customHex.of(255)); // Output: "0xff"


Type

Description

path

Path

```ts
import { createHasValue } from "@morpho-org/morpho-ts";

```

</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

[FieldType](#morpho-ts.fieldtype)<!-- -->&lt;T, Path&gt;

The value resolved at `path`<!-- -->, preserving nullish values from the input.

## Example


```ts
import { getValue } from "@morpho-org/morpho-ts";

const value = getValue({ user: { name: "Ada" } }, "user.name");

```

## hasValue() function

Tests whether a dot-separated path resolves to a non-nullish value.

**Signature:**

```typescript
hasValue: <T, Path extends PartialDottedKeys<T> = PartialDottedKeys<T>>(data: T, path: Path) => data is T & { [path in Path]: NonNullable<FieldType<T, path>>; }
```

Type

Description

data


</td><td>

T


</td><td>

Object to inspect.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

path


</td><td>

Path


</td><td>

Dot-separated path to read from `data`<!-- -->.

<a name="morpho-ts.mergeentries"></a>

## mergeEntries() function

Builds a record from entries, merging duplicate keys.

**Signature:**

```typescript
mergeEntries: <K extends PropertyKey, T>(srcEntries: Iterable<readonly [K, T]>, merger: (prev: T, value: T) => T) => Record<K, T>
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

srcEntries


</td><td>

Iterable&lt;readonly \[K, T\]&gt;


</td><td>

Iterable of key-value entries.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

merger


</td><td>

(prev: T, value: T) =&gt; T


</td><td>

Combines the previous value with a duplicate value.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

Record&lt;K, T&gt;

A record containing the merged entries.

## Example


```ts
import { mergeEntries } from "@morpho-org/morpho-ts";

const result = mergeEntries(
  [["a", 1], ["a", 2]],
  (prev, value) => prev + value,
);
// { a: 3 }
```

<a name="morpho-ts.numberformatter"></a>

## NumberFormatter class

A formatter for numeric values.

The `NumberFormatter` class provides functionality to format numbers according to various configurable options such as decimal precision, locale, unit, and more. It supports methods for customizing the formatting behavior and returns formatted strings based on the input value and settings.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare class NumberFormatter extends CommonFormatter
```
**Extends:** [CommonFormatter](#morpho-ts.commonformatter)

## Example 1

// Basic usage const formatter = formatter; console.log(formatter.of(1234.567)); // Output: "1234.567"

## Example 2

// Customizing decimal places const formatterWithDigits = formatter.digits(2); console.log(formatterWithDigits.of(1234.567)); // Output: "1234.57"

## Example 3

// Adding a unit const formatterWithUnit = formatter.unit("$"); console.log(formatterWithUnit.of(1234.56)); // Output: "$1234.56"

A formatter for percentage values.

The `PercentFormatter` class formats numeric values as percentages by multiplying the input value by 100. It supports customization options like decimal precision, locale, and more for tailored output.

<a name="morpho-ts.registercustomaddresses"></a>

## registerCustomAddresses() function

Registers custom addresses, deployment blocks, and unwrapped token mappings.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare function registerCustomAddresses<const TAddresses extends Record<number, unknown> = Record<never, never>, const TDeployments extends Record<number, unknown> = Record<never, never>>(options?: {
    unwrappedTokens?: Record<number, Record<`0x${string}`, `0x${string}`>>;
    addresses?: RegistryInput<TAddresses, keyof typeof _addressesRegistry, ChainAddresses, ChainAddressRegistration>;
    deployments?: RegistryInput<TDeployments, keyof typeof _deployments, ChainDeployments, ChainDeploymentRegistration>;
}): void;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

options


</td><td>

{ unwrappedTokens?: Record&lt;number, Record&lt;\`0x${string}\`, \`0x${string}\`&gt;&gt;; addresses?: RegistryInput&lt;TAddresses, keyof typeof \_addressesRegistry, [ChainAddresses](#morpho-ts.chainaddresses)<!-- -->, ChainAddressRegistration&gt;; deployments?: RegistryInput&lt;TDeployments, keyof typeof \_deployments, [ChainDeployments](#morpho-ts.chaindeployments)<!-- -->, ChainDeploymentRegistration&gt;; }


</td><td>

_(Optional)_ Optional configuration object


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

void

Nothing.

## Exceptions

RegistryValueAlreadyRegisteredError when registration attempts to override an existing value.

IncompleteChainRegistryError when a custom-chain entry does not include the required Blue registry fields.

## Remarks

Parameter details:

- `options.unwrappedTokens`<!-- -->: A mapping of chain IDs to token address maps, where each entry maps wrapped tokens to their unwrapped equivalents.

- `options.addresses`<!-- -->: Custom address entries to merge into the default registry. Known-chain entries may be partial; custom-chain entries must include the required Blue addresses and may add Midnight fields beside `blue`<!-- -->, `bundler3`<!-- -->, and other periphery addresses.

- `options.deployments`<!-- -->: Custom deployment entries to merge into the default registry. Known-chain entries may be partial; custom-chain entries must include the required Blue deployments and may add Midnight fields beside `blue`<!-- -->, `bundler3`<!-- -->, and other periphery deployments.

## Example


```ts
import { registerCustomAddresses } from "@morpho-org/morpho-ts";

registerCustomAddresses({
  addresses: {
    31337: {
      blue: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001",
      bundler3: {
        bundler3: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000002",
        generalAdapter1: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000003",
      },
      adaptiveCurveIrm: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000004",
      midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000005",
      midnightBundles: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000006",
      midnightMempool: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000007",
      ecrecoverRatifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000008",
      ecrecoverAuthorizer: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000009",
      setterRatifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000010",
      permit2: "0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3",
    },
  },
  unwrappedTokens: {
    31337: {
      "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000005": "0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE",
    },
  },
});
```

<a name="morpho-ts.retrypromiselinearbackoff"></a>

## retryPromiseLinearBackoff() function

Retries an asynchronous operation with a linear backoff delay.

**Signature:**

```typescript
retryPromiseLinearBackoff: <R>(func: () => R, options: {
    timeout?: number;
    retries?: number;
    onError?: (error: unknown, index: number) => unknown | Promise<unknown>;
}) => Promise<R>
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

func


</td><td>

() =&gt; R


</td><td>

Operation to execute until it succeeds or retries are exhausted.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

options


</td><td>

{ timeout?: number; retries?: number; onError?: (error: unknown, index: number) =&gt; unknown \| Promise&lt;unknown&gt;; }


</td><td>

Optional retry settings.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

Promise&lt;R&gt;

The resolved operation result.

## Remarks

Parameter details:

- `options.timeout`<!-- -->: Base delay in milliseconds multiplied by the retry attempt number.

- `options.retries`<!-- -->: Maximum number of retry attempts.

- `options.onError`<!-- -->: Optional hook called after each failure. Return a truthy value to stop retrying.

## Example


```ts
import { retryPromiseLinearBackoff } from "@morpho-org/morpho-ts";

const value = await retryPromiseLinearBackoff(async () => "ready", {
  retries: 2,
  timeout: 10,
});
// "ready"
```

<a name="morpho-ts.shortformatter"></a>

## ShortFormatter class

A formatter for compact numeric values.

The `ShortFormatter` class formats numbers in a short or compact notation, such as `1.2k` for thousands or `3.4M` for millions. It is useful for presenting large numbers in a concise and readable manner. This formatter supports customization options like decimal precision, units, and readability for small values.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare class ShortFormatter extends CommonFormatter
```
**Extends:** [CommonFormatter](#morpho-ts.commonformatter)

## Example 1

// Basic usage const formatter = formatter; console.log(formatter.of(1234567.89)); // Output: "1.23M"

## Example 2

// Customizing decimal places const formatterWithDigits = formatter.digits(1); console.log(formatterWithDigits.of(1234567.89)); // Output: "1.2M"

## Example 3

// Enabling small values with commas const formatterWithCommas = formatter.smallValuesWithCommas(); console.log(formatterWithCommas.of(1234.56)); // Output: "1,234.56"

## transformValue() function

Applies a transform to a defined value while preserving nullish inputs.

**Signature:**

```typescript
transformValue: <T, R>(value: T | null | undefined, _transform: (v: T) => R) => R | null | undefined
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

value


</td><td>

T \| null \| undefined


</td><td>

Value to transform.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

\_transform


</td><td>

(v: T) =&gt; R


</td><td>

Transform applied only when `value` is defined.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

R \| null \| undefined

The transformed value, or the original `null` or `undefined` input.

## Example


```ts
import { transformValue } from "@morpho-org/morpho-ts";

const value = transformValue(2, (x) => x * 3);
// 6
```
